title: Introduce egress fragment aggregation and tool-call handshake retries to stabilize streaming surface
author: Liam Chen
description:
Motivation: production incidents have shown two recurring failure modes for streaming tool/func calls via the OpenAI-compat gateway: (1) high fragmentation of small egress frames (many tiny chunks) causing excessive per-request overhead and intermittent credit exhaustion on constrained routes; (2) brittle first-handshake exchanges for fn/tool calls where transient network hiccups lead to unsupported partial handshakes and aborted streams. Both cases manifested as elevated 5xx/error rates and user-visible truncated fn-call outputs.

Goals: reduce noise and tail latency from fragmented egress, make fn/tool handshake more reliable without sacrificing compatibility, and surface metrics to validate behaviour. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) egress fragment aggregation: the proxy aggregates small outgoing chunks destined for the same client into coalesced frames up to a tunable size/TTL window (default 128KB or 15ms), reducing per-frame overhead and improving route credit utilization; 2) handshake retry policy for tool/function calls: add idempotent handshake retries with exponential backoff (configurable max_retries=3, initial_backoff_ms=50) and an explicit handshake token to allow safe replay across retries; 3) soft-route-payload enforcement during active tool calls: while a tool call is in-progress we allow a thin soft buffer above the per-route payload limit (configurable percent) and emit a "route_soft_limit_hit" metric rather than immediately rejecting the request — this prevents premature truncation for long-running tool outputs while still giving operators a signal to tighten limits.

What changed (summary): commits introduce a new egress_aggregator component in gateway/, handshake retry state machine in gateway/handshake.go, compatibility mappings in compat/openai_adapter.go to surface retryable errors as OpenAI-compatible transient errors, and test coverage for lost-first-packet scenarios. Small docs and changelog updates to explain tunable knobs and migration notes included.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind feature flag gateway.egress_aggregation and handshake_retries; default enabled in canary infra for 72h with metric checks. Observability: added metrics gateway.egress.aggregated_chunks, gateway.handshake.retries_{total,success,failure}, and gateway.route.soft_limit_events, all exported via Prometheus and surfaced in a new Dashboard tile in Console.

Testing: unit tests for the aggregator + deterministic TTL, integration tests simulating packet loss and delayed ACKs, and an e2e smoke against the OpenAI-compat adapter were added. Local perf benchmark on a c5xlarge-equivalent showed ~12% reduction in per-token CPU cycles and 8% lower p99 latency under small-chunk workloads.

Backward compatibility and safety: handshake retry uses an explicit idempotency token exchanged during the initial handshake so retries are safe even for non-idempotent tool endpoints (adapter must verify token or reject). Soft-limit behaviour is opt-in and defaults to conservative values; operators can opt-out by setting gateway.route.soft_limit_percent=0.

Migration notes: operators upgrading to this version should: (1) enable the canary flag for a subset of routes, (2) monitor gateway.route.soft_limit_events and route credit usage for 72h, (3) increase handshake_retries only after verifying downstream tool endpoints accept the idempotency token (most Redwood-adapted tool integrations do).

Checklist:
- [x] Add egress aggregation implementation and unit tests
- [x] Implement handshake retry state machine + integration tests
- [x] OpenAI-compat adapter error mapping updates and e2e smoke tests
- [x] Add Prometheus metrics and Console dashboard tile
- [x] Feature gating and rollout playbook in docs

Related: ENG-842 (stabilize streaming tool surface), PM-319 (reduce user-facing truncations).

review_comments: Anya Patel (reviewer): Please ensure the default soft-limit percent is documented prominently in ops and make the metric name consistent with existing route_* metrics. Also suggest adding a histogram for aggregated chunk sizes.
Author (Liam Chen): Addressed: doc updated and metric renamed to gateway.route.soft_limit_events; added gateway.egress.aggregated_chunk_size histogram. See updated tests. Thanks for the catch.
Miguel Santos (reviewer): Can we bound memory used by the aggregator per-connection? If many clients burst, aggregation buffers could spike. Suggest per-conn cap + global backpressure counter.
Author (Liam Chen): Added per-connection cap (default 1MB) and global backpressure metric gateway.egress.backpressure_count; aggregator will flush immediately on cap hit. Tests added.
ci_summary: All checks passed: unit, integration, lint; ephemeral perf job completed and attached. One flaky integ test rerun was required but passed on retry.
notes_for_merge: Gate enabled behind flags; need to coordinate canary roll as described in docs/ops/gateway-rollout.md. Ops has been pinged (linear ENG-842).
release_notes: Improve stability for streaming tool/function calls: coalesce small outgoing chunks, add handshake retry policy for transient network failures, and introduce soft-route-payload events to reduce premature truncation. Feature gated; enable incrementally during canary.
impact_summary: Expected positive impact on p99 tail for small-chunk workloads and lower transient truncation errors for tool calls. Operators must watch route soft-limit metrics after rollout.
qa_checklist: Unit tests added; integ sim for packet-loss; manual smoke against OpenAI-compat conducted; perf microbench shows improvement; recommend 72h canary with metric alerts before global enablement.
